candidate_relations.reason: Squamous cell carcinoma is a neoplastic epidermal tumor, not an abrupt neutrophilic dermal infiltrate with leukocytosis.
Wegener granulomatosis is a necrotizing granulomatous vasculitis; the biopsy showed no vasculitis and imaging was unremarkable.
Arthropod-bite reaction can be neutrophilic locally but does not produce multiple enlarging plaques on neck and both forearms with peripheral neutrophilia.
Bowen disease is intraepidermal carcinoma and would not show a dense dermal neutrophilic infiltrate without epidermal change.
Keratoacanthoma may mimic central depression clinically, but histology here is dermal neutrophilic edema, not a crateriform squamous proliferation.
Pyoderma gangrenosum is a related neutrophilic dermatosis that ulcerates; these lesions are firm nontender plaques, not ulcers.
Sweet syndrome matches abrupt plaques, dermal neutrophilic infiltrate without vasculitis, and 13,000 leukocytes with 89% neutrophils.
Eosinophilic cellulitis (Wells) is eosinophil-rich; the infiltrate here is neutrophilic without mention of eosinophils.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Wells eosinophilic cellulitis vs neutrophilic Sweet

candidate_relations.reason: Ordinary dermatitis does not produce a dense neutrophilic dermal infiltrate, marked edema, and peripheral neutrophilia.
Erythema multiforme is an interface/targetoid reaction, not a vasculitis-negative neutrophilic dermatosis of plaques.
Neutrophilic urticaria produces evanescent wheals, unlike firm 5-day enlarging plaques with striking central depression.
Neutrophilic dermatosis of the dorsal hands is a Sweet variant confined to hands; lesions here involve both forearms and the nape.
Neutrophilic dermatosis is the histologic family and omits the Sweet syndrome diagnosis.
Sweet's syndrome is the same acute neutrophilic dermatosis documented by biopsy without vasculitis.
Leukocytoclastic vasculitis is excluded by the explicit statement that the biopsy showed no vasculitis.
Vasculitis as a diagnosis conflicts with marked dermal neutrophilia and edema without vessel-wall necrosis.
Erythema elevatum diutinum is a chronic fibrosing neutrophilic vasculitis of extensor surfaces, not a 5-day eruption without vasculitis.
Neutrophilic dermatosis of the hands again localizes incorrectly; neck crusted plaques and forearm lesions define classic Sweet distribution.

case_quality_flags: The patient was afebrile, so classic febrile Sweet is incomplete on that single criterion, but histology and neutrophilia still support Sweet syndrome.
